Rashi on Nedarim 26b:1:1.hebrew: אלא סיפא - דרישא, דאמר לזה ולזה, הותר הראשון הותרו כולן, כדקתני לה. ורבי עקיבא היא ולא רבנן, כדקתני כיצד א"ר עקיבא וכו', ומשמע דפליגי רבנן עליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:1:1.english: But the latter clause - of the first clause [of the Mishnah], where he said, "To this one and to that one," [the law is that once] the first is permitted, all of them are permitted, as it teaches it. And it is [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva and not the Rabbis, as it teaches, "How did Rabbi Akiva say [it], etc.," which implies that the Rabbis disagree with him.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:1:2.hebrew: והא אמרת - היכא דאמר "הייתי אומר פלוני ופלוני אסורין", כולן מותרין. והשתא לא דייק "סיפא", אלא סיפא דרישא. והשתא לא מצי רבא לאוקמא לדברי הכל, דב"כולן אסורין" ליכא מאן דפליג, אפילו ר"ע, אבל הכא דקתני "הותרו כולן", רבנן פליגי עליה:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:1:2.english: But haven’t you said - Where one said, "I would have said so-and-so and so-and-so are prohibited," all of them are permitted. And now [the Gemara] is not being exact [in saying] "the latter clause," rather [it means] the latter part of the first clause. And now Rava cannot establish it as [the view of] everyone, for regarding [the case of] "all of them are prohibited," there is no one who disagrees, not even Rabbi Akiva; whereas here, where [the Mishnah] teaches "all of them are permitted," the Rabbis disagree with him.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:2:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רבא לרב פפא ולרבה מי ניחא סיפא - דסיפא, דקתני וכולן אסורין, במאי מוקים לה? דאמר לכולכם:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:2:1.english: Rava said to Rav Pappa: And according to Rabbah, does the latter clause work out well - For [regarding] the latter clause, where it teaches, "and all of them are forbidden," in what [case] does he establish it? [In a case] where he said, "To all of you."

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:2:3.hebrew: הדין הוא ראשון והדין הוא אחרון - הא לכולכם קתני סתם, ומאי ראשון ומאי אחרון איכא, דקתני האחרון מותר וכולן אסורין:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:2:3.english: Which one is first and which one is last - Behold, it states "to all of you" without specification; so what "first" and what "last" is there, that [the Mishnah] teaches: "The last one is permitted and all of them are forbidden"?

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:3:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - אנא מתרצינא להדדי דלא קשיא כלל, דסיפא דקתני ראשון ואחרון, לא משמע כדקתני שאיני נהנה לזה ולזה:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:3:1.english: Rather, Rava said - I harmonize them together so that there is no difficulty at all, for the latter clause, which teaches "first" and "last," does not mean [a case] as it teaches, "that I will not derive benefit from this one and from that one."

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:3:2.hebrew: אלא כגון שתלאן זה בזה - דמעיקרא אמר קונם שאיני נהנה לזה, והדר אמר פלוני יהא אסור כפלוני שהדרתי, ופלוני השלישי יהא אשור כשני. לפיכך קתני: הותר הראשון — הותרו כולן, שכולן תלויין בו; הותר האחרון — האחרון מותר וכולן אסורין, שהרי הראשון והאמצעי לא נתלו באחרון, לפיכך לא הותרו השנים בהתירו של אחרון:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:3:2.english: Rather, [it is] for example where he linked them to one another - For originally he said, "Konam that I will not benefit from this one," and then he said, "So-and-so shall be prohibited like so-and-so whom I forbade by vow," and the third [one], so-and-so, shall be prohibited like the second. Therefore [the Mishnah] teaches: [If] the first one was permitted, all of them are permitted, since all of them are dependent upon him; [if] the last one was permitted, the last one is permitted and all [the others] are prohibited, for the first and the middle ones were not made dependent upon the last one; therefore, the [first] two are not permitted through the permitting of the last one.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:4:1.english: It is also precise - That this is so, for that baraita teaches.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:4:2.english: [If] the middle one was permitted, from him and below is permitted - And this means he and the last one, who is dependent on him, are permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:4:3.hebrew: ממנו ולמעלה - היינו הראשון אסור, לפי שהן תלויין בו והוא אין תלוי בהן:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:4:3.english: From him and above - That is, the first one is prohibited, because they are dependent on him and he is not dependent on them.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:5:1.english: But isn't the kuferi [onion] - An onion of that place.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:5:2.english: He is permitted [with regard to] kuferi [onions] - For he only vowed [to abstain] from that which is bad for the heart, and not [with regard to] kuferi [onions].

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:5:3.english: And Rabbi Meir dissolved it - For he holds [that] a vow that was dissolved in part is dissolved in its entirety.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:6:1.hebrew: מאי לאו דאמר אילו הייתי יודע שהכופרי יפה ללב הייתי אומר כל הבצלין אסורין וכופרי מותר - דהיינו דומיא דכולכם אסורין חוץ מאבאואפ"ה התירו ר"מ בכל הבצלים, וקשיא בין לרבה בין לרבא. דאילו לרבה, בכולכם לא פליגי דאסור, והכא קא שרי ר"מ היכא דאמר בכולכם. ולרבא קשיא, דאמר בכולכם פליגי, דב"ש דאסרי סברי לה כר"מ:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:6:1.english: What, is it not where he said, "Had I known that the kuferi [onion] is good for the heart, I would have said, 'All onions are forbidden and kuferi is permitted'" - That is similar to [the case of], "All of you are forbidden except for my father," and even so Rabbi Meir permitted him [to benefit] from all the [other] onions. And [this] is difficult both according to Rabbah and according to Rava: for according to Rabbah, in [the case of] "all of you" they do not disagree that it is forbidden, whereas here Rabbi Meir permits [it] where he said "all of you." And according to Rava it is difficult, for he said that in [the case of] "all of you" they disagree, [and] Beit Shammai, who forbid, hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Nedarim 26b:7:1.hebrew: תריץ לה באומר אילו הייתי יודע שהכופרי יפה ללב הייתי אומר בצל פלוני ופלוני אסור וכופרי מותר - דהיינו פלוני ופלוני, ולהכי קא שרי ר"מ, והיינו דרבא דאמר פלוני ופלוני דברי הכל מותר, דר' מאיר אליבא דרבי עקיבא ואליבא דרבנן קא שרי, כלומר אליבא דד"ה, דהא ד"ה מותר. ותרווייה"ו גרי"ס המור"ה:
Rashi on Nedarim 26b:7:1.english: [The Gemara] resolves it [as a case] where one says, "If I had known that the kuferi [onion] is good for the heart, I would have said: Such-and-such onion and such-and-such [onion] are forbidden, and kuferi is permitted" - That is, [this is the case of] "such-and-such and such-and-such," and therefore Rabbi Meir permits [the other onions]. And this is in accordance with [the statement of] Rava, who said [that when one says] "such-and-such and such-and-such," all agree [that everything] is permitted; for Rabbi Meir permits [them] according to Rabbi Akiva and according to the Rabbis — that is to say, according to all opinions, for [according to] all opinions it is permitted. And the teacher reads both [in the text].

Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:2:1.hebrew: ולרבה מי ניחא סיפא במאי מוקים לה הדין הוא ראשון הדין הוא אחרון - כלומר, מ"ש ראשון ומ"ש אחרון? בתרוייהו הוה ליה למימר "הותרו כולן":
Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:2:1.english: And according to Rabba, does the latter clause work out well? In what [case] does he establish it? Which one is the first [and] which one is the last? - That is to say: what is the difference [between] the first and what is the difference [between] the last? In both [cases], it should have stated: "All of them are permitted."

Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:3:1.hebrew: אלא דרישא דאמר כולכם - ובהא פליגי רבנן ור"ע; דסיפא לאו מפלוגתא דרבנן ור"ע, אלא אפי' רבנן נמי מודו, וכגון שתלאן זה בזה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:3:1.english: Rather, the first clause is where he said, "all of you" - And in this [case] the Rabbis and Rabbi Akiva disagree; for the latter clause is not [part] of the dispute between the Rabbis and Rabbi Akiva, rather even the Rabbis also agree, and [it refers to a case] where he linked them one to another:

Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:5:1.hebrew: איתיביה רב אדא בר אהבה לרבא - בכולהו פירכי גרסינן לרבא, מיהו האי פירכא איתא לרבא, וכ"ש לרבה, כמו שאפרש בע"ה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:5:1.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava raised an objection to Rava - In all of the objections, we read [the text as] "to Rava"; however, this objection applies to Rava, and all the more so to Rabbah, as I will explain, with God's help.

Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:5:2.hebrew: קונם בצל שאני טועם - משנה היא בפרק ר' אליעזר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:5:2.english: "Onions are konam that I [will not] taste" - It is a Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer.

Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:5:3.hebrew: כופרי יפה ללב - על שם מקומו, וכן כלב כופרי. ובערוך פי' שהוא לשון כפר, שהוא של כפרים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:5:3.english: Kuferi is good for the heart - [It is named] after its place [of origin], and similarly [the phrase] "a kuferi dog." And in the Arukh, [the author] explained that it is from the term kefar [village], meaning that it is of the villages.

Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:6:1.hebrew: מאי לאו דאמר אילו הייתי וכו' כל הבצלים וכו' והתיר ר"מ - וקאמר: לדידך דקאמרת לעיל דב"ש אסרי משום תפוס לשון ראשון, וב"ש כרבי מאיר, והכא בהך ברייתא מתיר רבי מאיר אע"ג דסבר תפוס לשון ראשון! [ולרבה אמת קשה טפי] דלדידיה אמר לעיל "בכולכם" אסור לכ"ע, והא דפריך לרבא טפי — היינו משום שהיה תלמידו. ומשני: לא, באומר "אילו הייתי יודע הייתי אומר פלוני ופלוני", ור' מאיר אליבא דרבי עקיבא ואליבא דרבנן — כלומר: אליבא דכ"ע הוא, והיינו כרבא דאמר לעיל דהכל מודים באומר "לזה ולזה". ואליבא דרבה נמי לאו פירכא היא, די"ל דאליבא דרבי עקיבא אמר דוקא ולא אליבא דרבנן, דהא פליגי רבנן ב"לזה ולזה":
Tosafot on Nedarim 26b:6:1.english: What, is it not [a case] where he said: "Had I [known...], all onions [are forbidden...]," and Rabbi Meir permitted [them] - And [Rav Adda bar Ahava] says [to Rava]: According to you, who said earlier that Beit Shammai prohibit [them] because of [the principle] "seize the first expression," and Beit Shammai hold in accordance with Rabbi Meir — yet here in this baraita Rabbi Meir permits [all onions], even though he holds "seize the first expression"! [And in truth, it is even more difficult for Rabbah,] for according to him, he said earlier [that] in [a case of] "all of you" it is prohibited according to everyone; and the reason [Rav Adda bar Ahava] objects specifically to Rava is because he was his student. And [the Gemara] answers: No, [it is] where one says, "Had I known, I would have said such-and-such [an onion] and such-and-such [an onion]," and Rabbi Meir [rules] in accordance with Rabbi Akiva and in accordance with the Rabbis — that is to say, it is in accordance with everyone; and this is in accordance with Rava, who said earlier that all agree in [a case where] one says, "to this one and to that one." And according to Rabbah as well it is not a refutation, for one can say that [Rabbi Meir] stated [his ruling] specifically in accordance with Rabbi Akiva and not in accordance with the Rabbis, since the Rabbis dispute [the case of] "to this one and to that one."
